transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start: 15:02 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Meridian CTO), Morgan Lee (Meridian ML Eng), Samir Gupta (Meridian Platform)

Summary (auto-generated): Quick discovery about integration surface area; Meridian wants to understand how Redwood fits into their stack for both hosted and dedicated/private options, specifically around SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy setup, rate limits, and observability.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE. Priya on the line as well — SE who does a lot of the integration work. How's it going?
[00:05] Alex Rivera: Hey Jordan, good thanks. Morgan, Samir here too. We're excited to learn more, we've been looking at Redwood as a possible inference layer for a few services.
[00:12] Priya Patel: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: get background on your stack, constraints, which deployment modes you're considering (hosted/dedicated/private), and then walk through integration patterns — SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex, and observability. Sound good?
[00:22] Morgan Lee: Yeah that works. To set context, Meridian does clinical summarization pipelines and some real-time patient-facing assistants. We have strict PII rules, so data residency and encryption matter. Latency target is sub-300ms for our assistant, but for batch summarization latency is less critical.
[00:38] Samir Gupta: On infra we run in GCP us-east1, K8s, internal API gateway (Envoy), and we use a mix of serverless and long-running pods. Our ML infra team prefers to keep KV cache local when possible.
[00:50] Jordan Kim: Helpful. Are you initially leaning hosted or dedicated/private?
[00:53] Alex Rivera: We want to evaluate hosted for speed of launch but Dedicated or Private for production because of compliance and traffic predictability. Curious what the integration differences look like.
[01:02] Priya Patel: Sure — at a high level: Hosted is just our REST API / SDKs; very little infra on your side. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput, and Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you customer-managed network + KMS/HSM options. Integration-wise, SDKs are the same across modes, but private deployments have additional network steps (VPC peering or private link) and certs.
[01:22] Morgan Lee: On SDKs — do you have official SDKs for Python/Node, and any first-class support for LangChain or LlamaIndex?
[01:28] Priya Patel: Yes we have official Python and Node SDKs. For LangChain and LlamaIndex, we publish adapters/examples — they work against the Redwood API and include streaming and function-calling patterns. We also have a reference repo that Priya will share after the call.
[01:41] Jordan Kim: Also to note — many customers use our SDKs behind their own gateway or proxy so they can add auth, rate limiting, and observability hooks closer to their stack.
[01:50] Samir Gupta: That sounds like our model — we want the gateway to handle authentication and add tracing. Any recommended patterns?
[01:56] Priya Patel: Common pattern: your gateway authenticates callers, terminates TLS, and forwards to Redwood with a service credential. If you want request-level observability, you can pass our request-id headers and backpropagate them into your traces. We also provide tracing hooks and sample middleware for Envoy/NGINX.
[02:14] Morgan Lee: For LangChain, we use chains that call a couple of different models plus an embedding service. How does Redwood handle routing when you have mixed requests (embed vs generate)?
[02:22] Priya Patel: We support embeddings and generation endpoints. You can route by endpoint in your app or use our unified SDK that exposes both. For Dedicated, you can pin models to capacity pools and set routing policies — e.g., cheaper quantized model for embeddings, higher-quality for generation. Fallbacks are supported if capacity is constrained.
[02:38] Alex Rivera: Good. What about LlamaIndex — we use its chunking/indices. Do you recommend any config to keep costs down?
[02:44] Priya Patel: Yes — prefix KV caching and chunk-level caching help. Also we have quantization profiles and recommend batching for embedding calls. For LlamaIndex specifically, you can cache embeddings in your DB and only re-embed on content change. We'll send a starter guide for LlamaIndex patterns.
[02:59] Jordan Kim: Can you share a bit about rate limits and quotas? Our app has peaks and sustained traffic. We need both soft limits and hard quotas per team.
[03:07] Priya Patel: Hosted accounts have account-level rate limits plus per-key quotas. We expose token-level rate limits (requests per minute and tokens per minute) you can configure for dedicated pools. For Dedicated, you buy reserved throughput; we support burst capacity. We can also expose per-route quotas via the console so you can throttle certain product routes.
[03:26] Samir Gupta: Do you provide local proxying to avoid egress for private deployments? Our security team wants no egress for PHI.
[03:32] Priya Patel: For Private on-prem we run in your network — no egress. For VPC-based private deployments we support private link or peering so traffic stays within your VPC and we integrate with your KMS for key management.
[03:44] Morgan Lee: Observability — what hooks do you provide? We need spans, request-level IDs, per-token timing for latency breakdowns, and cost attribution.
[03:53] Priya Patel: Our observability suite includes per-request token-level latency, per-route dashboards, and hooks for OpenTelemetry. You can ingest our traces into your tracing backend; we provide request and token metrics via Prometheus metrics endpoint for Dedicated/Private. We also have a web console that breaks down cost by token bucket and route.
[04:10] Alex Rivera: If we put Redwood behind our gateway, will we lose streaming? We rely on streaming for live assistants.
[04:15] Priya Patel: Streaming works fine through a proxy if you configure it to support chunked transfer/websockets. We include examples for Envoy and NGINX configuration; crucial to make sure the proxy doesn't buffer the stream.
[04:26] Samir Gupta: Any thoughts on embedding cache TTLs or eviction with heavy update churn?
[04:31] Priya Patel: TTLs depend on how often your corpus updates; for high-churn content, shorter TTLs or per-update invalidation works. We support prefix invalidation APIs to clear relevant KV cache entries.
[04:41] Jordan Kim: Let's talk about a concrete benchmark. Morgan, can you share your target qps and seq lengths?
[04:46] Morgan Lee: Sure — baseline: 50 qps during peak, avg generation seq len 180 tokens, embeddings 10 qps, avg embed size 512 dims. Peaks may go to 120 qps for short bursts.
[04:58] Priya Patel: Perfect — for that profile we'd suggest a Dedicated pool with autoscale and a small burst buffer, plus prefix caching for assistant prompts. We'll size GPUs based on seq length and token throughput. We'll include a reference TCO in the pricing doc.
[05:12] Alex Rivera: For compliance, we need SOC2 evidence, encryption at rest + in transit, and audit logs. How mature is Redwood around that?
[05:20] Jordan Kim: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, supports customer-managed KMS in Private, and audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private. We'll share the security pack and a point-by-point checklist.
[05:30] Samir Gupta: On billing and quotas — can we get line items per route or per team? We want to show cost center breakdowns to finance.
[05:36] Jordan Kim: Yes the console has per-route cost breakdown and you can tag projects. We can export CSV billing for cost allocation.
[05:43] Morgan Lee: A couple of practical questions: 1) Do you have SDK examples for LangChain chains that do multi-step tool calls? 2) Any limits on function-calling size?
[05:51] Priya Patel: 1) Yes we'll include LangChain chain examples and a demo repo. 2) Function-calling payloads have size limits based on tokens — typical max payload is documented; for Dedicated we can increase limits with config, and for Private it's configurable depending on your infra. We'll share exact numbers in the integration doc.
[06:09] Alex Rivera: If we start with Hosted for a pilot then move to Dedicated, how seamless is the migration?
[06:16] Priya Patel: Very seamless — same API/SDKs and model catalog. For Dedicated you'll need to configure routing/pinning and set up network connectivity, but application code needs minimal changes.
[06:25] Jordan Kim: Great. Any blockers on your side for the bench?
[06:27] Morgan Lee: We'll need an NDA in place before we share some internal logs, and we'll compile a traffic sample for Priya to size the benchmark. Also need to loop in security for the checklist.
[06:37] Jordan Kim: Understood. We'll get the security pack and NDA over.
[06:40] Priya Patel: I'll share the LangChain/LlamaIndex starter repo and Envoy proxy examples after the call. Also will propose a benchmark plan for the week of 11/15.
[06:49] Alex Rivera: Cool — for the benchmark, could you include a mix of streaming assistant load plus batch summarization?
[06:54] Priya Patel: Absolutely — we'll include both scenarios and show latency & cost tradeoffs.
[06:58] Samir Gupta: One small note — our platform team uses OpenTelemetry and Grafana; is there an easy integration?
[07:04] Priya Patel: Yes we provide OTLP exporters and Prometheus metrics; we can help map the schema.
[07:09] Jordan Kim: Ok wrapping up — recap of next steps: Jordan send pricing/TCO, Priya send integration repos and envoy examples, Meridian share traffic sample and security contacts, schedule benchmark week of 11/15. Anything else?
[07:21] Alex Rivera: That's it from us. Thanks.
[07:23] Jordan Kim: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with artifacts.

End of transcript.
